idea.title: Separate capturing content opportunities from approving them
idea.summary: Refined the Content OS lifecycle so project agents preserve moderately screened raw ideas in an inbox, while a distinct editorial qualification gate decides whether each idea deserves production.

context.goal: Align Content OS workflow documentation with the existing file-based idea capture practice and approved production lifecycle.
context.situation: Project agents already capture potentially useful opportunities into content/ideas after primary work is complete and verified, but Workflow 01 was still named Idea Discovery and treated recent-work scanning as its normal production entrypoint.
context.problem: The capture inbox and editorial publication decision were blurred across workflow and lifecycle documentation, risking stricter capture or unqualified ideas reaching Content Planning.
context.investigation: Compared the playbook, capture rules, lifecycle, architecture/product descriptions, Brand Strategy, Posted Titles, idea schema, and content-strategist skill. Found that the three-verdict gate already existed, while the input contract and ownership boundaries were inconsistent.
context.decision: Keep capture intentionally moderate and raw; make Workflow 01 an editorial qualification gate with REJECT, DEVELOP, or READY; allow only a selected current READY idea into Workflow 02.
context.implementation: Updated workflow and lifecycle documentation, the strategist skill, and active README/architecture/product references. Kept Workflow 03 as canonical meaning ownership and Workflow 04 as platform/language adaptation ownership.
context.result: Documentation now separates capture/ingestion from production qualification and defines the handoff to Content Planning.

learning_points: A useful raw capture threshold and a strict publication-quality gate solve different problems and should have separate owners.
Moderately noisy capture can preserve authentic context without implying every saved idea should become a post.
Explicit workflow handoffs help prevent adjacent stages from repeating or silently replacing each other's decisions.
story_points: The system already had a strategist verdict gate, but the workflow name and entrypoint still implied idea discovery.
The correction was primarily a contract/documentation alignment rather than an application feature.
The approved boundary preserves raw capture, adds editorial qualification, then allows only READY ideas into planning.
possible_angles: Why a capture inbox should not double as a publishing approval queue.
Separating evidence-preserving idea capture from editorial qualification.
How explicit stage ownership prevents workflow gates from being duplicated downstream.

notes: This is a raw capture, not a qualification verdict or publish-ready content direction.
The change was documentation and skill-contract alignment; no renderer, Studio, export, layout, or schema behavior changed.
